memory_candidates.content: When a reader's filter argument type mismatches a schema's declared field type (e.g. jq --argjson against a field the schema types as string), the mismatch can silently zero out every downstream read that depends on the filter matching -- including unrelated field-name mismatches that would otherwise be visible. A single type-insensitive diagnostic comparison run alongside (never feeding) the strict filter, warning on divergence, catches this class of defect on its first occurrence instead of letting it survive silently for an unbounded number of runs. Keep the diagnostic textually co-located with the strict filter inside the same query program so a reviewer sees both and they cannot drift apart.

The no-task-references-in-deliverables write-time hook scans only the new_string/content payload of a single Edit/Write call, not the surrounding file -- a fixture edit that lands inside an already-open task-ref-ok:begin...end block elsewhere in the file still gets blocked unless the edit's own new_string carries its own marker (or the whole edit is performed via a non-Edit-tool mechanism, e.g. a Bash/python in-place rewrite, which the hook does not intercept). When editing task-citing fixture content inside an existing exempt block via the Edit tool, wrap just the edited hunk in its own inline task-ref-ok:begin/end pair rather than relying on the file-level block.
